subject: toucan
reasoning:
I'm planning out a toucan model using the SDK, aiming for a compact but realistic design—around 0.55m long with a perched height of 0.4m, standing upright with feet at floor level. I'm working out the joint hierarchy starting with hips as the root, positioning the skeleton to support a natural resting pose facing forward.

I'm sketching a spine chain running from hips through chest and neck to the head, using a series of points to define the curve with named joints at each segment. Then I'm figuring out how to loft the body parts along this chain to build the toucan's torso and neck shape.

For the body I'm using a sweep along the spine chain with a radius function that bulges in the middle and tapers toward the tail and head, giving an egg-like upright profile. For coloring I'm planning a paint function that applies black over most of the body, a yellow-white bib on the chest, and red near the undertail coverts based on position conditions.

The head attaches as a sphere joint, black, then the massive toucan bill splits into upper and lower jaws as separate swept shapes with tapering radii following curved paths forward from the face, bound to head and jaw bones respectively, painted with a yellow-to-orange-to-black gradient along their length.

Now I'm placing the eyes with a blue skin patch, pale eye sphere, and black pupil mirrored on both sides of the head, then moving on to building the folded wing joints and their swept paths from the shoulders.

Switching to an extruded outline approach for the wing shape instead, orienting the 2D profile so the outward normal points correctly for the left wing.

Working out the wing outline coordinates...

Now I'm setting up the wing bone chain with shoulder, wrist, and tip joints, attaching it as a chain bone parented to spine2, then extruding the wing geometry weighted to those joints.

For placement, I'm positioning the wing against the body's curved surface at around x=0.09-0.095 to keep it separate, deciding to leave the pose vertical rather than angling it outward for simplicity. For coloring, I'm going with a simple dark palette (#17171c) with a slightly smaller secondary layer rather than adding stripes or gradients.

For the tail, I'm planning a short chain of segments curving back and down from the hips, roughly 0.17m long, held at a slight downward angle consistent with a perched posture where the body leans upright around 45 degrees.

Writing sweep geometry...

For coloring, I'm thinking mostly black tail feathers with a possible red undertail patch on the underside, maybe handled through sector-based painting rather than a full separate mesh.

I'm adding the undertail covert patch as a small flattened red sphere near the body's underside, then working out the leg structure—short thick hip-to-foot chains for the zygodactyl feet, positioning joints so the toucan stands properly on the floor.

Now I'm figuring out the toes: two forward and two back per foot, modeled as thin tapered capsule rods angled outward from the foot point so their tips just touch the ground plane.

Each toe becomes a simple two-point chain parented to the foot joint, since a two-point polyline gives a single span that's easy to sweep. For the leg itself I'm using a three-point path so it bends properly, with the chain's first joint tied to the root at the hips. Then I'm setting up the head chain as the tip of the spine chain.

The spine chain runs through four joints (spine1, spine2, neck, head) built from a catmull path, giving three spans plus the tip for the head sweep. For the torso sweep I'm defining a radius function that bulges around the chest, tapers toward the hips and neck, and relies on round caps to blend into the head and legs, while I work out the width versus depth values using the spine's local coordinate frame.

Now I'm writing the paint function for the torso surface — it checks position and normal to assign a cream-white throat bib with a yellow edge transition, layered over the base plumage color.

Writing color blend logic...

Still refining color masks...

Setting up the head as a sphere mesh positioned and scaled onto the head bone, keeping the black crown with cream throat gradient.

For the bill, I'm defining a curved catmull-rom path running from the face forward, with tapering width and height functions to create that tapered toucan bill shape with a ridged profile, rounded at the base and tip.

Still refining bill curve coordinates...

Now I'm planning the bill coloring: orange base with a black spot at the tip and a red line at the base, matching a toco toucan's bill pattern.

I'm adding a small nostril detail using approximate surface coordinates, then working out placement for a blue eye patch as an ellipsoid positioned on the head's curved surface, calculating the radius based on the sphere's cross-section at that height.

Then I'm positioning the eye itself: a dark pupil sphere with a tiny white highlight slightly offset for a glint effect, and a surrounding skin patch, before setting up a mirror loop to replicate these features symmetrically on both sides.

Now I'm working out the wing geometry - plotting curve points for the wing extending from the body near the tail, checking that it clears the body radius and tail span, and setting up the extrusion direction so the shape mirrors correctly for left versus right sides.

Unifying the sign convention so both wings share one formula with a flip factor, then adding a wing bone for the shoulder joint and planning extra covert feather layers with darker iridescent outlines slightly offset outward.

Now I'm settling on simpler colors: dark base wing, lighter covert blue, bluish-grey legs and toes. For the tail I'm sketching a flattened sweep shape with dark banding, then realizing toucans have a distinctive white rump patch, so I'm adding a conditional paint rule to turn the body white where it's near the back and upper body.

Still working out the body paint logic... Then I'm setting up the jaw joint attached to the head, planning to use a sweep path for the upper bill bound to the head bone and the lower bill bound to the jaw bone, and starting to define the skeletal chain structure.

Now I'm defining the spine chain and root joint position, then setting up leg chains ending in foot joints, and adding toe chains branching off each foot with tapered sweep radii for the digits.

Counting joints total around 27, which works. I'm defining the leg as a three-point polyline from hip to ankle to foot, skipping claws and nail details for simplicity, and keeping the throat minimal before moving on to writing the actual code with color constants.

For paint, I'm using a mix function that blends two colors based on position and normal, applying it to shade the head darker toward the top with cream underneath. I'm placing the head sphere just past the neck tip and letting the body's sweep connect smoothly into it before returning the root bone structure.
